propositions.canonicalProposition: The candidate moved the front-end build to Vite and added Lighthouse CI with per-route performance budgets to the pull-request pipeline.
propositions.rationale: The resume describes the build migration and the pipeline budgets directly.

propositions.canonicalProposition: The candidate fixed keyboard navigation and screen-reader labels in the drag-and-drop task board after an external WCAG 2.1 AA audit, and the findings were closed in September 2023.
propositions.rationale: The resume states the fixes and the reference check confirms them and the closure date in writing.

propositions.canonicalProposition: The candidate's code-splitting work made the dashboard load 2.3x faster for every customer.
propositions.rationale: The figure appears on the candidate's own demo slide next to one Lighthouse run, with no baseline build, date range or field data; under the quantification rule a figure without a defined baseline is not evidence, and the 'every customer' attribution is not stated by any measurement.

expectedGap: The dashboard speed-up on the demo slide has no baseline build, date range or field measurement behind it.
expectedBoundaryNote: Report the virtualised timeline, the build and budget work, the code-splitting change and the audit fixes as documented; record the slide's speed-up figure as an unsupported claim with a follow-up about the comparison.
permittedFollowUpTargets: Ask which build the dashboard was compared against, over what date range, and whether the comparison used lab runs or real-user monitoring data.
